content.title: About
content.content: Ham or pork with stuffing is a boiled or smoked pork product that is filled with various fillings (such as breadcrumbs, spices, vegetables, or mushrooms). It is commonly used in festive dishes, appetizers, and sandwiches. The product offers a juicy flavor, aromatic spices, and a pleasant texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Stuffing meat dates back to ancient times and was popular in European cuisine.
Ham with stuffing is often prepared as large loaves that are later sliced thinly.
Different regions use unique mixtures: Poland – sauerkraut, Italy – cheese and herbs, Russia – buckwheat and onion.
Smoking gives the product its characteristic aroma and extends shelf life.
Ham with stuffing is frequently served cold as an appetizer, but it can also be reheated in the oven.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Pork provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Ham contains thiamine, riboflavin, niacin, and vitamin B12, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The product supplies iron, zinc, and phosphorus, important for blood formation and bones.

items.title: Satiety
items.content: The combination of protein and fat helps maintain a feeling of fullness longer.

items.title: Benefits of spices
items.content: Fillings often include garlic, paprika, or herbs, which have antioxidant properties.

items.title: High salt content
items.content: Ham is often salty; excessive salt intake can raise blood pressure.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Pork contains saturated fats that may affect cholesterol levels when consumed frequently.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Some hams may contain nitrites and other preservatives, which raise concerns for certain consumers.

items.title: Allergy to spices
items.content: Fillings can include nuts, seafood, or other allergens.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Ham with stuffing can be eaten cold as sliced meat, added to salads, sandwiches, and appetizer platters. It can also be gently warmed in the oven or on a skillet to enhance the spice aroma.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store ham in its original packaging or an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0 °C to +4 °C. It keeps up to 7 days after opening. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C, where it retains quality for up to 3 months.
